chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah, from Abu Umayyah Yusuf ibn Thabit ibn Abu Sa'dah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: Faith (Iman) is such that no deed harms it, and similarly, Disbelief (Kufr) is such that no deed benefits it.

key_terms.الْإِيمَانُ: Faith, belief in God and the prophets

ai.seo_question: Does sin destroy faith or do good deeds save disbelief?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the Shia doctrine of 'Iman al-Muqarrar' (firm faith), where the core conviction remains intact despite minor sins, contrasting with the view that faith can be lost through disbelief. It underscores that while good deeds do not compensate for fundamental rejection of truth (Kufr), they also do not nullify the essential bond of faith in a believer who commits sins, provided the core belief remains. This distinction is crucial in Shia theology for understanding the status of sinners (Ahl al-Fusq) who are not considered disbelievers.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba, from Abu Ameyt Yusuf Bin Sabi Bin Abu Sa’da,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Emān is such that no deed would harm along with it, and similar to that is the Kufr (disbelief), no deed would benefit along with it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Faddal from Tha’labah from abu ‘Umayyah, Yusuf ibn Thabit ibn abu Sa’dah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
With belief no deed can harm one and with disbelief no deed can benefit one.’”
